60.. Items not on the posted agenda, to be presented and (if requested) referred to staff or placed on the agenda for action at a future meeting of the Board, or matters requiring immediate action.  ..minute     Supervisor Yaroslavsky made the following statement:

     “In response to the potential threat of bio-terrorism, the State and County emergency medical system agencies and public health departments throughout the Country have moved to a level of alertness that parallels the current mobilization among federal, state and local law enforcement agencies.

     “We are fortunate in Los Angeles County to employ a highly professional emergency medical and public health workforce at the front lines in any threat to the health of our communities.  We are also privileged to have working in the Department of Health Services and among the local health industry, universities and research organizations, highly reputable experts on the identification, distribution and treatment of biological agents as potential weapons of bio-terrorism.  Many of these experts fulfill various responsibilities regarding the planning and preparedness for bio-terrorism events in Los Angeles County.

     “Several of these experts were active participants in the recent State sponsored conferences on bio-terrorism held in Ontario and Burbank, and have helped educate all of us concerning these biological agents through print, radio and television interviews.  Most of these experts maintain communication with one another through their professional linkages and as advisors to various emergency medial and public health committees.

     “However, there is no existing forum that brings these experts together in a more structured setting for the specific purpose of advising the Board on matters related to our overall preparedness for bio-terrorism.  This should be corrected with the formation of a formal County Task Force on Health Services Preparedness for Bio-Terrorism.  One of the keys to protecting the public from acts of bio-terrorism is the existence of strong system of medial surveillance and reporting.  Early detection and treatment of individuals affected by such an event is critical to their survival.  

     “While the Department of Health Services maintains an active surveillance program, it is critical that the medical community is provided the on-going education necessary to recognize the results of a bio-terrorism incident.  Los Angeles County has been a leader in disaster preparedness in this nation.  We must now ensure that we are equally ready to identify and respond to any potential acts of bio-terrorism.”

     Therefore, Supervisor Yaroslavsky made a motion that the Board take the following actions:

1.     Make a finding pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(b)(2), that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action came to the attention of the Board subsequent to the agenda being posted as specified in subdivision (a);

2.     Instruct the Director of Health Services to convene a group of experts on bio-terrorism as The Los Angeles County Task Force on Health Services Preparedness for Bio-terrorism, with the Task Force to review the County's preparedness for a bio-terrorism event, and recommend whatever actions and programs are necessary, including funding, to assure the highest level of readiness with regard to the bio-terrorism threat, and to include academic and other experts in the field to meet regularly and continue on throughout the duration of the Nation's war on terrorism; and

3.     Instruct the Acting Director of Health Services to:

a.     Identify the availability of funds in the Department of Health Services budget that could be reallocated to initiate the enhancement of existing bio-terrorism surveillance activities, such as school absenteeism, veterinary surveillance, private hospital emergency visits, private physician visits, and pharmaceutical stocks;

b.     Prepare a plan for a public education campaign designed to increase public awareness of bio-terrorism preparedness and encourage greater compliance among the medical community for surveillance and reporting;

c.     Work in consultation with the Chief Administrative Officer to identify and seek additional federal resources to further support and expand these activities; and

d.     Report back to the Board on actions taken in response to this motion at the October 16, 2001 Board meeting.

     Supervisor Burke made a suggestion that Supervisor Yaroslavsky motion be amended to also instruct the Acting Director of Health Services to develop a policy for quarantine of County residents consistent with the standards and authority of the Federal health officers and report back to the Board with a proposal for provision of safe areas for County employees in the event of an emergency.  Supervisor Yaroslavsky accepted Supervisor Burke's amendment.
